findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated as a detector handler
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` but does not implement the abstract methods `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. It therefore remains an abstract class. `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` references this class, and `Detector.detector_handler` will do `group_type.detector_handler(self)`. For any detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire`, processing will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler ...` instead of evaluating. Either implement the required methods or avoid registering this unsupported handler until it is implemented.

findings.title: Evaluation crashes for stateful detectors with no counters
findings.body: `get_state_data` only populates `counter_updates` inside `if self.counter_names:`. When a concrete `StatefulDetectorHandler` defines `counter_names = []` (a valid stateful detector with no Redis counters), `counter_updates` remains `{}`. The `DetectorStateData` construction then accesses `counter_updates[gk]` for each group key and raises `KeyError`, so evaluating any data packet with group values fails. Use `counter_updates.get(gk, {})` or default each group key to `{}`.

findings.title: Evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring on `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` still says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`, but the method now returns a dict keyed by `DetectorGroupKey`. This is misleading for implementers and callers after the signature change.

findings.title: Mock occurrence builder ignores `value`, so the new hook's value argument is not verified
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value: int` but never uses it when constructing the expected `IssueOccurrence` or `event_data`. Because expected results in tests such as `test_state_results`, `test_results_on_change`, and `test_dedupe` are built through this helper, those tests would pass even if `evaluate_group_key_value` passed the wrong value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. The helper should incorporate `value` into the expected occurrence/event data, or tests should assert the hook call received the correct value.
